projectDir.description: Directory holding the project, relative to the directory the CLI runs in.

version-declared.name: Clojure version is declared
version-declared.description: The project depends on the Clojure release it builds against, and that release is no older than the configured floor.
version-declared.remediation:
Add a Clojure dependency where the project already declares its dependencies:

```clojure
{:deps {org.clojure/clojure {:mvn/version "1.12.0"}}}
```

Leiningen takes the same coordinates in `:dependencies`. If the project names no Clojure version, it compiles against whichever release the installed tool falls back to, so the language version a build uses depends on the runner, not on the commit.

minVersion.description: Oldest Clojure version accepted. A declared version below this is a violation.

dependencies-pinned.name: Clojure dependencies are pinned
dependencies-pinned.description: Every dependency in the manifests names a single released version, or the exact commit a git dependency builds from.
dependencies-pinned.remediation:
Name a specific release, and give every git coordinate the sha it resolves to:

```clojure
{:deps {cheshire/cheshire {:mvn/version "5.13.0"}
        io.github.company/queue {:git/url "https://github.com/company/queue"
                              :git/tag "v1.4.0"
                              :git/sha "6f3a1c2d9b8e4f7a0c5d2e1b3a4f5c6d7e8f9a0b"}}}
```

`RELEASE`, `LATEST` and `-SNAPSHOT` resolve to whatever the repository serves at the moment the build runs, and a `:git/url` without a `:git/sha` resolves to wherever the branch has moved since. Either way, the artifact you ship is not the one that was reviewed.

repositories-allowed.name: Repositories are ones the team allows
repositories-allowed.description: Every Maven repository the manifest adds beyond the defaults resolves from a host on the allowed list.
repositories-allowed.remediation:
Resolve only from hosts your team has vetted, and give every repository entry the URL it resolves from:

```clojure
{:mvn/repos {"clojars" {:url "https://repo.clojars.org/"}}}
```

Add an internal mirror to `allowedHosts` instead of leaving it unnamed. An unvetted repository is exactly what a dependency confusion attack needs: if someone publishes a package under your coordinates on a host the build can reach, the build resolves it as if it were yours. An entry with no `:url` tells you nothing about where its artifacts come from.

allowedHosts.description: Comma separated hosts a repository may resolve from. A repository on any other host is a violation.

no-local-dependencies.name: No dependencies on a local root
no-local-dependencies.description: No dependency comes from a `:local/root`, so the build resolves everything from this commit and not from the machine it runs on.
no-local-dependencies.remediation:
Publish the library and depend on its published coordinates, or bring its source into the checkout:

```clojure
{:deps {company/queue {:mvn/version "1.4.0"}}}
```

A `:local/root` builds from a directory outside the checkout. The build works on the laptop that happens to have that directory next to it, and anywhere else it either fails or compiles different code.
